comment: Tables provided by osquery extensions shipped with the GLPI agent. Merged into the upstream osquery catalogue by QueryCatalog::load() so the live-query console offers them like any other table. Keep in step with agent/cmd/*-ext.

tables.name: glpi_edid
tables.description: Monitor EDID blocks read from /sys/class/drm. Provided by the glpi-edid extension bundled with the GLPI osquery agent — it is not part of osquery, and returns nothing on a stock osqueryd. Exists because osquery has no monitor table on Linux and no way to read the raw bytes.

columns.name: path
columns.description: Full sysfs path to the EDID file, e.g. /sys/class/drm/card1-DP-2/edid

columns.name: data
columns.description: Raw EDID block, hex encoded. Shaped to match the Windows registry EDID value so one decoder serves both platforms.

columns.name: connector
columns.description: Connector the panel is attached to, e.g. DP-2, eDP-1, HDMI-A-1

columns.name: bytes
columns.description: Length of the EDID block; 128 per block, so 384 means two extension blocks

columns.name: preferred_mode
columns.description: Mode the kernel prefers, e.g. 5120x1440. Trusted over decoding the EDID, because a native timing may live in a DisplayID extension block.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Connector state as reported by the kernel: connected or disconnected

tables.name: glpi_block_stack
tables.description: Linux block-device stack read from /sys/class/block, as lsblk sees it. Provided by the extension bundled with the GLPI osquery agent. Exists because osquery's disk_encryption leaves `encrypted` blank for every NVMe and device-mapper node, which is where a standard LVM or LUKS install keeps its root filesystem.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Kernel device name, e.g. dm-0 or nvme0n1p3

columns.name: device
columns.description: Device node, e.g. /dev/dm-0

columns.name: dm_name
columns.description: Device-mapper name, e.g. ubuntu--vg-ubuntu--lv; mounted as /dev/mapper/<dm_name>

columns.name: dm_uuid
columns.description: Device-mapper UUID. CRYPT-LUKS2-… is a LUKS2 volume, LVM-… a logical volume

columns.name: kind
columns.description: crypt, lvm, physical or other

columns.name: parents
columns.description: Comma-separated devices immediately beneath this one

columns.name: encrypted
columns.description: 1 if this device or anything beneath it is dm-crypt, 0 if the stack resolved with no crypt layer, empty if it could not be resolved

columns.name: crypt_device
columns.description: dm name of the crypt layer found beneath, if any

tables.name: glpi_battery
tables.description: Batteries read from /sys/class/power_supply, in GLPI's units. Provided by the extension bundled with the GLPI osquery agent, because osquery's battery table exists only on macOS and Windows. Peripheral batteries (mice, headsets) are excluded.

columns.name: name
columns.description: Kernel name of the supply, e.g. BAT1

columns.name: manufacturer
columns.description: Battery manufacturer

columns.name: model
columns.description: Battery model name

columns.name: serial
columns.description: Battery serial number

columns.name: technology
columns.description: Chemistry, e.g. Li-ion

columns.name: status
columns.description: Charging, Discharging, Full or Not charging

columns.name: cycle_count
columns.description: Charge cycles, where the firmware reports them

columns.name: capacity_percent
columns.description: Current charge as a percentage

columns.name: design_capacity_mwh
columns.description: Capacity when new, in mWh; converted from charge using the design voltage when the kernel reports µAh

columns.name: full_capacity_mwh
columns.description: Capacity when fully charged today, in mWh

columns.name: voltage_mv
columns.description: Design minimum voltage, in mV, or the present voltage when that is not reported

tables.name: glpi_chassis
tables.description: System chassis from DMI (/sys/class/dmi/id). Provided by the extension bundled with the GLPI osquery agent, because osquery's chassis_info exists only on Windows.

columns.name: chassis_type
columns.description: SMBIOS chassis type code, e.g. 10 for a notebook

columns.name: chassis_name
columns.description: The code's SMBIOS name, e.g. Notebook, Desktop, Rack Mount Chassis

columns.name: vendor
columns.description: Chassis vendor

columns.name: serial
columns.description: Chassis serial number (readable by root only)

columns.name: asset_tag
columns.description: Chassis asset tag
